proposals.before: Zhang Guan was a man of Chedu Village in Tongzhou, a nephew by marriage of the former Taiyuan military overseer Zhang Chengye.
proposals.after: Zhang Guan was a man of Chedu Village in Tongzhou, a nephew of the former Taiyuan military overseer Zhang Chengye.
proposals.reason: 猶子 means a brother's son / nephew treated as a son, not a nephew by marriage.

proposals.before: During Tang Tianyou Chengye served the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong with distinction and won great trust. When Guan heard of his success, he and his five brothers left their village for Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong gave them all posts.
proposals.after: During Tang Tianyou Chengye served the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong with distinction and won great trust. When Guan heard of his success, he and his brothers—five in all—left their village for Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong gave them all posts.
proposals.reason: 昆仲五人 conventionally means a group of five brothers including the subject, not the subject plus five additional brothers.

proposals.before: When Emperor Shao of Jin faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard. After the emperor's return he was made military governor of Fuzhou and soon after honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: When Emperor Shao of Jin faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard. After the emperor's return he was made regent of Fuzhou and soon after honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 鄜州留後 is an acting regency (留後), not a full military-governor (節度使) appointment; elsewhere this chapter renders 留後 as regent.

proposals.before: When Jin's Emperor Shao faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard; when the carriage returned he was appointed military governor of Fuzhou, and soon after given honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: When Jin's Emperor Shao faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard; when the carriage returned he was appointed regent of Fuzhou, and soon after given honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise over-translates 留後 as military governor; regent matches the office term.

proposals.before: Under Mingzong he commanded the left wing of the Pingsheng Guard while also holding the prefecture of Hezhou.
proposals.after: Under Mingzong he commanded the left wing of the Pengsheng Guard while also holding the prefecture of Hezhou.
proposals.reason: 捧聖 is Pengsheng, not Pingsheng; 捧 is peng.

proposals.before: In Mingzong's time he was commander of the left wing of the Pingsheng Guard and concurrently held the prefecture of Hezhou.
proposals.after: In Mingzong's time he was commander of the left wing of the Pengsheng Guard and concurrently held the prefecture of Hezhou.
proposals.reason: Same mistranscription of 捧聖 as Pingsheng instead of Pengsheng.

proposals.before: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Khitan violated the capital, Jianxiong regent Liu Zaiming had an audience with the Khitan and made deputy commissioner Luo Zhilang administer the prefectural affairs.) End supplemental note.〉
proposals.after: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Khitan violated the capital, Jianxiong regent Liu Zaiming had an audience with the Khitan and made deputy commissioner Luo Zhilang administer the prefectural affairs.)
proposals.reason: Trailing English editorial gloss and stray bracket are not in the Chinese and corrupt the literal rendering.

proposals.before: The Liang forces then pressed hard against the southern camp, chaining warships across the river to block reinforcements and attacking day and night for three days. The camp commander Shi Yanzhang sent urgent word to Zhuangzong.
proposals.after: The Liang forces then pressed hard against the southern camp, chaining warships across the river to block reinforcements and attacking day and night for three days. The camp commander Shi Yanshang sent urgent word to Zhuangzong.
proposals.reason: 氏延賞 ends in 賞 (shǎng); Yanzhang wrongly reads 賞 as if 張.

proposals.before: It happened that the Liang army urgently attacked the south stockade, linking warships midstream to cut off the relief route; they assaulted the city day and night for three days, and the stockade commander Shi Yanzhang reported emergency to Zhuangzong.
proposals.after: It happened that the Liang army urgently attacked the south stockade, linking warships midstream to cut off the relief route; they assaulted the city day and night for three days, and the stockade commander Shi Yanshang reported emergency to Zhuangzong.
proposals.reason: Same error: 賞 is shang/shǎng, so Shi Yanshang not Shi Yanzhang.

proposals.before: The court at once made Wan military commissioner of Huazhou, but rewarded Lu Shunmi far more generously.
proposals.after: The court at once made Wan military commissioner of Huazhou, but rewarded Lu Shunmi only meagerly.
proposals.reason: Chinese 酬之甚淺 means the reward to Lu Shunmi was very slight; the idiomatic English reverses the sense to 'far more generously'.

proposals.before: Early in Kaiyun he was posted to Meizhou.
proposals.after: Early in Kaiyun he was posted to Fuzhou.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou; the idiomatic place name is wrong.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was sent out to hold Meizhou.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was sent out to hold Fuzhou.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou; the literal place name is wrong.

proposals.before: In year 3 he returned to govern Meizhou.
proposals.after: In year 3 he returned to govern Fuzhou.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou.

proposals.before: In the third year he again garrisoned Meizhou.
proposals.after: In the third year he again garrisoned Fuzhou.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou.

proposals.before: Early in Yingshun he was made military commissioner of Meizhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: Early in Yingshun he was made military commissioner of Fuzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Yingshun he was transferred to military commissioner of Meizhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Yingshun he was transferred to military commissioner of Fuzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou.

proposals.before: When Mingzong of Tang was military commissioner of Daizhou, he appointed Li as a yamen officer; Li followed him through successive provincial commands.
proposals.after: When Mingzong of Tang was prefect of Daizhou, he appointed Li as a yamen officer; Li followed him through successive provincial commands.
proposals.reason: 刺代州 means served as prefect (cishi) of Daizhou, not as military commissioner (jiedushi).

proposals.before: The one highest in armor among the generals was made regent.) End supplemental note.〉
proposals.after: The highest-ranked among the generals was made regent.) End supplemental note.〉
proposals.reason: 甲 here marks seniority/rank among the generals, not physical armor; the literal rendering 'highest in armor' misreads the selection criterion stated in the note.

proposals.before: During Jin Kaiyun, when the Khitan pressed Chanzou, Peng served as vanguard overseer, charged the enemy at personal risk, was wounded, and withdrew.
proposals.after: During Jin Kaiyun, when the Khitan pressed Chanzhou, Peng served as vanguard overseer, charged the enemy at personal risk, was wounded, and withdrew.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou; 'Chanzou' is a misspelling that obscures the place name.

proposals.before: In Kaiyun of Jin the Khitan pressed Chanzou; Peng was vanguard overseer, threw himself forward to strike the enemy, was wounded, and returned.
proposals.after: In Kaiyun of Jin the Khitan pressed Chanzhou; Peng was vanguard overseer, threw himself forward to strike the enemy, was wounded, and returned.
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou; the literal line repeats the same misspelling 'Chanzou'.

decisions.reason: Focus unit 承業之猶子也 uses 猶子 for a brother’s son / nephew treated as a son, not an affinal ‘nephew by marriage.’ The proposed ‘nephew’ matches the Chinese and the chapter’s idiomatic for the same unit.
Focus unit 與昆仲五人 names a five-brother group including Guan, not Guan plus five additional brothers. The proposed ‘brothers—five in all’ removes that overcount while keeping the rest of the sentence.
Focus unit 授鄜州留後 is a 留後 acting appointment, not a full 節度使. Elsewhere this chapter renders 留後 as ‘regent’ (e.g. s0109); replacing ‘military governor’ with ‘regent’ restores the office term.
Same focus phrase 授鄜州留後; the literal likewise over-translates 留後 as ‘military governor.’ ‘Regent of Fuzhou’ matches the Chinese office.
Focus unit 捧聖左廂都指揮使 begins with 捧 (pěng); ‘Pingsheng’ wrongly reads it as if 平. ‘Pengsheng Guard’ is the accurate transcription.
Literal repeats the same 捧聖 → Pingsheng error; Pengsheng matches 捧.

decisions.after: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Khitan violated the capital, Jianxiong regent Liu Zaiming had an audience with the Khitan and made deputy commissioner Luo Zhilang administer the prefectural affairs.)〉
decisions.reason: The English gloss ‘End supplemental note.’ is not in the Chinese and must go, but the closing 〉 belongs to the 〈…〉 note wrapper and is kept in the idiomatic for this unit; the proposal wrongly drops that bracket with the gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹犯闕，建雄留後劉在明朝於契丹，以節度副使駱知朗知州事。）〉

decisions.reason: Focus unit names 氏延賞; 賞 is shǎng, so the given name is Yanshang, not Yanzhang (as if 張). The proposed idiomatic name is correct.
Literal likewise misreads 賞 in 氏延賞 as zhang; Shi Yanshang restores the correct reading.
Focus unit 盧順密酬之甚淺 means Lu Shunmi’s reward was very slight; ‘far more generously’ reverses the sense. ‘Only meagerly’ restores the Chinese.
Focus unit 出授鄜州; 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fūzhōu), not Meizhou. The proposed place name is correct.
Literal of the same 出授鄜州 likewise needs Fuzhou, not Meizhou.
Focus unit 復鎮鄜州 again names Fuzhou; idiomatic Meizhou is wrong.
Literal of 復鎮鄜州 must read Fuzhou, not Meizhou.
Focus unit 遷鄜州節度使; 鄜州 is Fuzhou. Replacing Meizhou corrects the place name.
Literal of the same 鄜州 appointment likewise requires Fuzhou, not Meizhou.
Focus unit 唐明宗之刺代州 uses 刺 for prefect (刺史), not military commissioner (節度使). ‘Prefect of Daizhou’ matches the Chinese; the idiomatic already has the same sense.

decisions.after: The highest-ranked among the generals was made regent.)〉
decisions.reason: In 諸將之甲者, 甲 marks foremost rank, not armor, so that part of the proposal is right; but ‘End supplemental note.’ is still an invented English gloss absent from the Chinese, while the closing 〉 belongs to the note wrapper and should remain as in the idiomatic.
Focus unit 契丹迫澶州; 澶州 is Chanzhou. ‘Chanzou’ is a misspelling; the proposed fix is accurate.
Literal repeats the same 澶州 → Chanzou error; Chanzhou is correct.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepting r0005 shows the English office label inherited the mistranscription Pingsheng; 捧聖 requires Pengsheng while the Chinese office and evidence stay the same.
Accepting r0008 shows the English personal name Shi Yanzhang came from misreading 賞; the person remains 氏延賞, so the English value must be Shi Yanshang to match the pinyin already recorded.
